title: Vera Therapeutics Announces Positive ORIGIN 3 Final Efficacy Analysis of TRUTAKNA™ (atacicept-vymj) in IgA Nephropathy Presented at ASN Kidney Week 2026 and Published in the New England Journal of Medicine
summary: TRUTAKNA, the first and only FDA-approved BAFF and APRIL inhibitor, achieved statistical significance in all prespecified endpoints, including eGFR change from baseline and annualized slope, and risk reduction in composite kidney disease progression events.
body_markdown:
- *TRUTAKNA, the first and only FDA-approved BAFF and APRIL inhibitor, achieved statistical significance in all prespecified endpoints, including eGFR change from baseline and annualized slope, and risk reduction in composite kidney disease progression events.*
- *Favorable safety profile, and generally comparable to placebo.*
- *Plan to submit supplemental BLA to the U.S. FDA in Q4 2026 for full approval expected in 2027.*
- *Investor webcast is scheduled for October 22 at 4:30 pm EDT.*


BRISBANE, Calif., Oct. 22, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Vera Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: VERA), a commercial-stage biotechnology company, today announced that the final efficacy analysis for the ORIGIN 3 trial of TRUTAKNA in adults with primary IgA nephropathy (IgAN) at risk for disease progression was presented as a featured late-breaking oral presentation during the opening plenary session of the American Society of Nephrology (ASN) Kidney Week 2026 and simultaneously published in[The New England Journal of Medicine](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=MPes8-bshCzEVBOWXuJEnntvOAxdDG7YMfgIDwnrvq5Q0rPMEeAFOIsemAGJj92Cy0T3YR0h5giE77kFjs1iBzJoBQSo30S9wWJG4R-QwachvlzrDIqbqBaO0nlx3GKb) .


ORIGIN 3 met the primary endpoint of statistically significant proteinuria reduction at 36 weeks. In the final efficacy analysis, TRUTAKNA achieved statistical significance in all prespecified endpoints.


A photo accompanying this announcement is available at[https://www.globenewswire.com/NewsRoom/AttachmentNg/6f52e3a8-5843-4d89-a51b-a1344e2a52b3](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=gJpzjfE4maOLwSo_h5oVh7Q34Fzy-oydfgn5wIXUDMC_8AJH2ct4y-cd_okHO-71BcsqwSrh5D3UI9h4GvjSJ6Iu1LKX3Jb3DnWkDFsjmjRioNFw_lvEQc8BDCFCccDayMEamFaGGV_bOfTqqSqyKIJ653DTY35HXoTx5c2JUv2_i7yEjEZK5b7sUOYgc0zPacf92HsECx4dIGpXCrC2brlR-hs6egVgmBq3O36iyUMSNaPXfdoJGS1l0LcX56YgTq_P0voXAcNPTgBwJLLEwg==)


TRUTAKNA also achieved statistically significant reductions in urine-protein to creatinine ratio, galactose-deficient IgA1, and hematuria. TRUTAKNA was well tolerated with a favorable safety profile generally comparable to placebo, consistent with previous safety data from the ORIGIN program.1 Adverse events occurred in 160/214 patients (75%) on TRUTAKNA and 167/214 on placebo (78%). The rate of serious adverse events in the TRUTAKNA group was 7% compared with 15% in the placebo group. Infection rates were similar between TRUTAKNA (51.4%) and placebo groups (52.3%), and no clinically relevant hypogammaglobulinemia or opportunistic infections were observed. There was 1 death in the placebo group and no deaths in the TRUTAKNA group. No clinically meaningful effect of anti-drug antibodies on efficacy or overall safety was identified.


“I have spent my career caring for people with IgAN, and for most of that time, our conversations were about the limited treatment options," said Jonathan Barratt, PhD, FRCP, Mayer Professor of Renal Medicine, University of Leicester. "The ORIGIN 3 final efficacy results have the potential to change those conversations. In the study, TRUTAKNA achieved a physiologic rate of eGFR loss compared to the pathologic rate observed with placebo and significantly reduced the risk of composite kidney disease progression events, reflecting the potential for disease modification and kidney protection in IgAN. These results, combined with a safety profile comparable to placebo, represent a meaningful advance for patients."


“ORIGIN 3 represents an important innovation in IgAN clinical development through our alignment with the FDA on an earlier final efficacy analysis. As a physician, I value the ability to offer patients randomized to placebo an earlier opportunity to transition to open-label active treatment, while generating a robust dataset. With the strength of the clinical data package, TRUTAKNA has the potential to transform the treatment landscape,” said Marshall Fordyce, M.D., Founder and CEO of Vera Therapeutics. “We plan to submit the supplemental BLA in the fourth quarter of this year, and we look forward to potential FDA full approval of TRUTAKNA in 2027. We reiterate our gratitude to the patients, investigators, employees, and collaborators who have helped us to deliver TRUTAKNA to patients in need.”


The Company will host an investor call and webcast to discuss the trial results at 4:30 PM EST on October 22. To register, click[here](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=gywDDiiN0gZFCgsW0U06CDUgorknOx-_IF3zgt3qGTtic83W7dZ8vTkOD-S56c4hphSMdaouTc8iPDcbbwvTDewL7N5G4nbPDpC3lxAQYt4ZIwc1kulUepuFY42uTofn) .

**Indication**


TRUTAKNA (atacicept-vymj) is indicated to reduce proteinuria in adults with primary immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN) at risk for disease progression.


This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on reduction of proteinuria. It has not been established whether TRUTAKNA slows kidney function decline over the long-term in patients with IgAN. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in a confirmatory clinical trial.


**Important Safety Information**


Contraindications: TRUTAKNA is contraindicated in patients with serious hypersensitivity to atacicept-vymj or any excipients of TRUTAKNA.


**Warnings and Precautions**


Immunosuppression and Increased Risk of Infections: TRUTAKNA suppresses the immune system by reducing antibody production, which may increase the risk of infections. Patients with chronic infection or recurring infections may have an increased risk of serious infection. In clinical trials, infections were reported in 32% of TRUTAKNA patients compared with 28% of placebo patients.


Before initiating TRUTAKNA, assess patients for active infections. Delay TRUTAKNA administration in patients with active infection until the infection resolves or is adequately treated. Monitor patients for signs and symptoms of infection during treatment with TRUTAKNA. If a serious infection develops, consider interrupting TRUTAKNA until the infection is controlled.


The concomitant use of TRUTAKNA and other immune-modulating therapies has not been evaluated. Concomitant use of TRUTAKNA with drugs that affect the immune system, including systemic corticosteroids, may increase the risk of infection.


Immunosuppression and Immunization Risk: TRUTAKNA may interfere with the immune response to vaccines and increase the risk of infection from live vaccines. Prior to initiating treatment with TRUTAKNA, complete all age-appropriate immunizations. Live vaccines are not recommended within 30 days prior to initiation or during treatment with TRUTAKNA as safety of coadministration has not been established.


Adverse Reactions: The most common adverse reactions (≥5%) in patients treated with TRUTAKNA and placebo, respectively, were infections (32% vs 28%) and local administration reactions (30% vs 5%). The most common infection was upper respiratory tract infection (12% vs 9%), and the most common local administration reactions were injection site reaction (19% vs 2%) and injection site erythema (6% vs 1%).


**Use in Specific Populations**


Pregnancy: Available data on TRUTAKNA used in pregnant women exposed during clinical trials are insufficient to evaluate for a drug-associated risk of major birth defects, miscarriage, or other adverse maternal or fetal outcomes.


Based on the mechanism of action, TRUTAKNA may cause immunosuppression in the in utero-exposed infant. Consider the potential clinical impact of TRUTAKNA exposure in infants exposed in utero. Pregnant women exposed to TRUTAKNA, or their healthcare provider, should report TRUTAKNA exposure by calling 1-833-633-8372.


Pediatric Use: The safety and effectiveness of TRUTAKNA in pediatric patients have not been established.

**About TRUTAKNA (atacicept-vymj)**


TRUTAKNA, a B-cell activating factor (BAFF) and A proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL) inhibitor, is a soluble recombinant fusion protein containing the human transmembrane activator and calcium-modulating cyclophilin ligand interactor (TACI) receptor that binds to the cytokines BAFF and APRIL.2 BAFF and APRIL are key cytokines that activate B cells and drive IgAN pathophysiology. In IgAN, activated B cells produce both the antigen and associated antibodies that result in the production of damaging IgA immune complexes. The overlapping roles of BAFF and APRIL in activating B cells support the potential for TRUTAKNA as a disease-modifying therapy.3 TRUTAKNA is self-administered as an at-home, small-volume (1 ml), 150 mg once-weekly autoinjector.

**About IgAN**


IgAN is a serious, progressive, immune-mediated kidney disease and a leading cause of chronic kidney disease and kidney failure worldwide.3,4 Approximately 2.5 adults per 100,000 worldwide are diagnosed with IgAN each year, most often between 30 and 40 years of age.5,6 Over time, IgAN can lead to irreversible kidney damage and may ultimately require dialysis or kidney transplantation. At least 50% of patients may progress to kidney failure or death within 10 to 20 years of diagnosis.4


**About Vera Therapeutics**


Vera Therapeutics is a commercial-stage biotechnology company focused on the pursuit of truth in science to transform medicine in autoimmune disease, starting with the kidney. Vera Therapeutics’ flagship commercial product is TRUTAKNA (atacicept-vymj), a BAFF and APRIL inhibitor indicated to reduce proteinuria in adults with primary IgA nephropathy at risk for disease progression. Beyond IgAN, Vera Therapeutics is evaluating additional diseases where the reduction of autoantibodies through inhibition of BAFF and APRIL may prove clinically meaningful. Vera Therapeutics was founded in 2016 and is based in Brisbane, California.
